newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SOCCER-ZIMBABWE NATIONAL COACH PORTERFIELD QUITS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZIMBABWE NATIONAL COACH PORTERFIELD QUITS.

text.p: Zimbabwe national soccer coach Ian Porterfield said on Wednesday he would quit at the end of this month because of unwarranted criticism of his team.
The Scottish coach told state media he would not extend his six-month contract with the Zimbabwe Football Association (ZIFA) when it expires at the end of April because he had had enough.
Porterfield -- who helped rebuild the national team in neighbouring Zambia when their squad perished in a plane crash in 1993 -- has undergone heavy criticism since taking up the Zimbabwe job.

Local media have accused him of transforming the Zimbabwe side from an attacking outfit into an ultra-defensive team. But he dismisses the attacks, saying although he has some good players, he needs time to rebuild and to do a decent job.

Zimbabwe have lost three away matches, won three and drawn one home game under his charge in the African Cup of Nations and World Cup qualifiers, and the chances of the team qualifying for either of the two for the first time are slim.
"There is too much unwarranted criticism of the team here and it is unlike in Zambia where everyone was behind the team," he said.
Porterfield said he would leave the southern African state after its home match against Angola in the next World Cup qualifier on April 27.

"I am definitely going back home to see my wife and my children soon after the game against Angola. Even if Zimbabwe win 5-0 or even if I am offered a lot of money that will not count. I will be very happy to go home," he said.
ZIFA officials were unavailable for comment on Wednesday.
